claims.statement: MCP connections are HTTPS-only named records with either streamable HTTP or SSE transport, an explicit enabled flag and tool allowlist, encrypted headers and optional client-credentials OAuth; a record offers no tools unless its allowlist is nonempty.

Connection updates encrypt supplied headers and OAuth client secrets, cannot reuse saved credentials across names or silently retain headers after a URL change, and return only credential-free public fields by default.
Instance and workspace MCP records are persisted by tier in PostgreSQL while personal records are stored under user records; their owner-specific namespaces also key discovery and OAuth-token caches.
Run MCP sources are ordered instance, workspace, personal, then managed tools; for a shared connection name a later source replaces the complete earlier record.

MCP discovery is bounded to 30 seconds, rejects duplicate upstream names, caches catalogs by source namespace, connection name, and revision for ten minutes fresh and up to 24 hours total, and turns a per-connection discovery failure into an empty tool group.

Every MCP invocation reauthorizes the bound source and rereads the connection; it rejects disabled, scope-changed, endpoint-changed, or no-longer-allowlisted tools before creating a fresh client, and converts unexpected call failures to a safe ToolException.
Configured MCP OAuth uses encrypted client credentials to request and cache bearer tokens, supports client-secret-post and client-secret-basic, refreshes before expiry, and retries once after a 401.

Open SWE can serve a stateless remote MCP endpoint at /oswe/mcp using GitHub authentication; each request resolves the signed-in person's native and scoped integration tools, and execution reuses the private-thread ToolNode contract.

The remote MCP OAuth proxy stores cross-replica OAuth state in PostgreSQL, seals all fields not explicitly approved as plaintext with TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, hashes credential-like authorization-code keys, and treats expired or undecryptable entries as absent.

LangSmith Managed Tools is an instance-selected gateway loaded only for a private thread's credential owner with that owner's current LangSmith token; provider grants and tokens remain at LangSmith, and token unavailability drops only this managed source.

Managed Tools handles both all-services-required and partial gateway credential policies, exposes missing OAuth or secret credentials, mints consent links only for OAuth services, and refreshes its MCP catalog after a connection is made.

LangSmith LLM Gateway routing is optional and centralized in make_model: workspace configuration overrides the deployment default, supported provider prefixes receive gateway base URL and LangSmith credentials, and unsupported providers or missing gateway credentials fall back to direct calls.

Datadog request tracing is optional: API creation applies OPENSWE_ENV to Datadog when available, and middleware renames the current root span to the routed HTTP method and path while swallowing tracing-name failures.

Product analytics emits fail-soft, opaque-ID lifecycle events into a PostgreSQL outbox; worker delivery uses locked claims, acknowledgements, jittered exponential retries, and eventual dead-lettering.

Agent cost is a deferred LangSmith enrichment: a successful lookup records cost and thread metadata, while unavailable or failing lookups schedule bounded retries and eventually report unavailable/exhausted without changing the run outcome.

Focused tests cover MCP tier isolation, encrypted OAuth persistence and expiration, per-call scoped allowlist enforcement, remote-MCP access/schema behavior, Managed Tools credential and ownership flows, and model fallback resolution.
